subject: Dedicated capacity walkthrough — QPS & SLO alignment
messages:
From: Lena Park <lena@aurora-analytics.com>
To: sales@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-08-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: Dedicated capacity walkthrough for high-throughput inference

Hi Redwood team,

We just completed a self-serve trial and saw promising results for a portion of our inference workload. Aurora Analytics is interested in a Dedicated capacity walkthrough focused on throughput and latency guarantees — we expect sustained traffic for a customer-facing feature and need to understand how Dedicated would map to our QPS and SLOs.

Quick context:
- Model family: open-llm-13B variant
- Peak burst: ~420 QPS (90 requests/s sustained for short windows)
- Avg payload: 220 tokens in + 60 tokens out
- Target SLO: p95 < 450ms

Can someone from your SDR/solutions engineering team run a short session next week to walk our engineering leads through capacity sizing and canary strategies? Jorge (copied) will coordinate calendar times.

Thanks,
Lena Park
Director of ML Platform
Aurora Analytics

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Park <lena@aurora-analytics.com>
Cc: michael_grant@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-08-20T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Dedicated capacity walkthrough for high-throughput inference

Hi Lena — great to hear you had a good self-serve trial, and congrats on the momentum. I'm Ben from SDR at Redwood; we handle intake and scheduling for Dedicated walkthroughs.

A couple of quick asks so we can make the session productive:
- Please confirm whether the 420 QPS number is sustained or burst and the expected burst window (seconds).
- What percent of requests do you expect to be streaming vs. non-streaming?
- Would you like latency targets evaluated at p50/p95/p99? We typically size for p95 but can include the others.

Proposed 45-minute slots (PST):
- Tue Aug 22, 11:00–11:45
- Tue Aug 22, 14:00–14:45
- Wed Aug 23, 09:00–09:45

Also attaching a short capacity worksheet to capture a few workload details ahead of the call — filling that out beforehand helps the SRE/SE team prepare a tailored demo.

[Attachment: capacity-sizing-sheet.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

If none of those work, Jorge, please propose a time and we'll do our best to accommodate.

Best,
Ben Carter
Sales Development Representative
Redwood Inference
From: Jorge Rios <jorge@aurora-analytics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, michael_grant@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-08-21T08:29:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Dedicated capacity walkthrough for high-throughput inference

Thanks Ben — quick clarifications from our side:
- 420 QPS is a peak burst estimate; sustained expectation is ~95–120 QPS over 10–15 minute windows during heavy traffic. Burst windows rarely exceed ~60s.
- Streaming will be ~12% of requests.
- We'd like bandwidth on p95 and p99, with emphasis on p95 < 450ms.

All good for Tue Aug 22 at 11:00 PST — but can we push to 10:30 if there's an earlier SE? Our engineering leads prefer earlier blocks. I've filled out the worksheet and attached a short network topology diagram (not confidential).

Best,
Jorge
Head of Platform Engineering
Aurora Analytics

[Attachment: aurora-network-sketch.png (image/png)]

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
To: Jorge Rios <jorge@aurora-analytics.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-21T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Dedicated capacity walkthrough for high-throughput inference

Thanks Jorge — appreciate the details and for filling the worksheet. I'm Michael (Solutions Engineering). Naomi will run the technical portion of the walkthrough. Couple quick notes before the session so we can tailor the demo:

1) Sizing assumptions we'll evaluate during the call:
   - Token distribution you provided (220 in / 60 out)
   - Burst handling: pre-warmed pools vs autoscale behavior for ~60s bursts
   - KV cache/prefix reuse opportunities (if you have repeated prompts)

2) Pre-demo checklist (if you can confirm before 10:30):
   - Confirm whether requests are authenticated via a single service identity or multiple client identities (affects routing).
   - Share a small representative prompt set (5–10 examples) if you have privacy-safe samples — it helps with latency profiling.

Naomi — can you take 10:30–11:15 PST tomorrow? If not, 11:00 is fine; Ben will handle the calendar invite. I've attached our Dedicated playbook for reference.

[Attachment: redwood-dedicated-playbook.pdf (application/pdf)]

Hi Michael — 10:30 PST works better for us. Thanks for the pre-demo checklist; I'll send over a handful of redacted prompts and confirm auth patterns with our security lead.

One last ask: can we include a 10-minute slot at the end for costs/unit economics (what qps maps to what committed capacity and approximate monthly run-rate)? Our CFO will join remotely for that segment.

Sounds good otherwise — Jorge will accept the calendar invite.

Best,
Lena
Director of ML Platform
Aurora Analytics
